subject: Civil Engineering
title: Space Frames: 3D Trusses
description: A quick, practical guide to Space Frames: 3D Trusses.

hook.text: Airport terminals span huge areas with no columns. A 3D truss covers them.

buildup.text: Space frames extend the truss idea into three dimensions — tetrahedra or octahedra.

discovery.text: They spread loads in every direction, so no single bar carries too much force.

twist.text: A space frame can be incredibly light — the Louvre pyramid uses glass and thin steel.

climax.text: The Eden Project's biomes in Cornwall are giant space-frame geodesic domes.

punchline.text: Add a dimension to trusses and you can roof an entire stadium.

quiz.question: How do space frames differ from ordinary trusses?
options: They use curved members instead of straight bars
They extend the truss concept into three dimensions
They only work for underground structures

details.summary: Space frames are three-dimensional truss systems where interconnected members form a lightweight grid capable of spanning large areas in two directions simultaneously.
details.whyItMatters: Space frames provide long-span roof solutions with minimal material by extending the truss concept into three dimensions, creating column-free spaces for assembly buildings.
takeaways: Space frames distribute loads in two directions through a 3D network of members
Node connectors join multiple tube members at each intersection point
They cover large areas with relatively shallow depth and lightweight components

faq.question: How do space frames differ from planar trusses?
faq.answer: Planar trusses work in one direction, spanning between two supports like a beam. Space frames extend the triangulated network into three dimensions, distributing loads in multiple directions simultaneously.

faq.question: What caused the notable space frame roof collapses?
faq.answer: The Hartford Civic Center Coliseum roof collapsed in 1978 under snow load due to inadequate member sizes and connection eccentricities not accounted for in the original design. Space frame failures typically result from connection failures, underestimated loads, or buckling of compression members.
